key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the grounds that the accused-appellants reside in Pune, the distance between their residence and the place of trial at Patna is 1750 kms, and that they are not suffering from any physical illness.
bail_history: Anticipatory bail was granted to all the accused except Arnesh Kumar, husband of the complainant, on 21.06.2013
trial_duration: The Magistrate summoned the accused on 11.10.2012; the High Court dismissed the application on 17.04.2017; the Supreme Court allowed the appeal on 16.03.2018
legal_representation: Rakesh Kumar, Adv. for the Appellants; Ms. Abha R. Sharma, Abdullah, Advs. for the Respondents
appeal_history: Trial court: Order rejected; High Court: Application dismissed; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed
prosecution_argument: The State argued that the accused-appellants filed their application under Section 205 Cr.P.C. at a subsequent stage after appearing before the court, making it non-maintainable. They also emphasized that the nature of the offences required the presence of the accused and the complainant for conciliation.
defence_argument: The accused-appellants argued that their application under Section 205 Cr.P.C. was filed prior to their appearance in court and that the Magistrate failed to consider their grounds for exemption, which included the long distance between their residence and the place of trial, and their personal circumstances.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the Magistrate has the discretion to exempt the accused from personal appearance under Section 205 Cr.P.C. at any stage of the proceedings, provided the reasons are recorded.
